hypothesis: GQA group packing in the split-KV (decode) path: each split program handles one KV head and packs the GROUP query heads (x query positions) that share it into the M dimension (row r -> seq r//GROUP, head kvh*GROUP + r%GROUP), so every K/V tile is loaded once per KV head instead of once per query head. Grid becomes (num_splits, cdiv(Sq*GROUP, BLOCK_M)*Hkv, B); split count is recomputed from the packed base grid; workspace layout and combine kernel unchanged.
rationale: Decode rows are the worst vs FA2 (decode_65536 0.68x, 32768 0.81x, 16384 0.88x). Decode is memory-bound and currently each of the 4 q-heads in a group re-streams the same K/V (BLOCK_M=16 with 1 real row), so KV traffic is ~4x the minimum once the KV cache exceeds L2 (65536: 268 MB total KV). Packing makes 4 of 16 rows real and cuts K/V reads 4x; prefill path is untouched.
expected_effect: Large speedup on decode_16384..65536 (approaching DRAM roofline ~0.17 ms at 65536), modest gain on smaller decode rows; prefill unchanged. Geomean up several percent.
